info.name: Class 66 - Redis Streams: rescue within a consumer group
info.description:
One endpoint: **POST http://localhost:9020/orders** (order-service). Each call adds one entry to the Redis stream `orders`.

**Services:** order-service 9020 (producer), email-service 9021 (group email), delivery-service 9022 (group delivery).

**Before the first request:** `DEL orders` in redis-cli, then start email-service and delivery-service, then order-service.

Run the requests in order. Each one says what to do before sending and what to look for in the consoles.

request.description:
**Before:** order-service, email-service and delivery-service are running.

**Send** once.

**Expect:** the email console and the delivery console both print order 501.

**Why:** two groups (email, delivery), each with its own bookmark, so each gets every order.

**Before:** stop email-service (every copy). Keep delivery-service running.

**Send** once.

**Expect:** only delivery prints 502. Now start email-service again: it prints 502 as it starts.

**Why:** the order waits in the stream, and the email group's bookmark did not move. With Pub/Sub (class 63) this email was lost.

item.name: 3. Two email copies share the work - order 503

request.description:
**Before:** run a second copy of email-service with program arguments `--server.port=9023 --app.consumer-name=email-2`.

**Send** 4 or 5 times, changing the id each time (503, 504, 505...).

**Expect:** each order is printed by only ONE of the two email consoles. Delivery prints all of them.

**Why:** both copies are in group email, so they share one bookmark: each order is handed out once.

item.name: 4a. Crash BEFORE the email is sent - order 510

request.description:
**Setup:** email-1 started in **Debug** mode (bug icon). email-2 started with **Run** (not Debug), program arguments `--server.port=9023 --app.consumer-name=email-2`. A Run copy ignores breakpoints, so only email-1 pauses. Restart both copies after adding PendingRescuer.

**Breakpoint:** `EmailListener`, on the `System.out.println("EMAIL SERVICE -> sending confirmation...")` line.

**Send** until email-1 pauses at the breakpoint (if email-2 prints it instead, change the id and send again).

**Then:** within 60 s, press the red **Stop** on email-1's Debug tab. That is the crash.

**Expect:** 60-90 s after sending, email-2 prints `rescued entry ... from email-1`, then the email line. Sent once.

**Why:** PendingRescuer runs every 30 s in each copy and claims entries stuck over 60 s.

**Check:** redis-cli `XPENDING orders email - + 10` shows the stuck entry and its owner. After the rescue, `XPENDING orders email` is 0.

item.name: 4b. Crash AFTER the email is sent, before XACK - order 520

request.description:
**Setup:** email-1 started in **Debug** mode (bug icon). email-2 started with **Run** (not Debug), program arguments `--server.port=9023 --app.consumer-name=email-2`. A Run copy ignores breakpoints, so only email-1 pauses. Restart both copies after adding PendingRescuer.

**Breakpoint:** `EmailListener`, on the `acknowledge(...)` line.

**Send** until email-1 pauses. It has already printed the email line.

**Then:** within 60 s, press **Stop** on email-1.

**Expect:** 60-90 s later email-2 rescues it and prints the email line AGAIN. Sent twice.

**Why:** Redis only knows 'no XACK'. It cannot tell that the email went out. Streams are at-least-once: make the work safe to repeat.

**Check:** redis-cli `XPENDING orders email - + 10` shows the stuck entry and its owner. After the rescue, `XPENDING orders email` is 0.

**Setup:** email-1 started in **Debug** mode (bug icon). email-2 started with **Run** (not Debug), program arguments `--server.port=9023 --app.consumer-name=email-2`. A Run copy ignores breakpoints, so only email-1 pauses. Restart both copies after adding PendingRescuer.

**Breakpoint:** `EmailListener`, on the `System.out.println(...)` line.

**Send** until email-1 pauses.

**Then:** do NOT stop email-1. Wait more than 90 s, then press **Resume** on email-1.

**Expect:** while email-1 is paused, email-2 rescues it and prints the email. After Resume, email-1 prints it too. Sent twice.

**Why:** Redis cannot tell slow from dead. The 60 s limit (STUCK_AFTER) must be longer than the slowest normal send.

**Check:** redis-cli `XPENDING orders email - + 10` shows the stuck entry and its owner. After the rescue, `XPENDING orders email` is 0.
